skill.name: awesome-bug-bounty
skill.description: Guides authorized bug bounty research with scoped methodologies, vulnerability references, payload examples, tool selection, installation guidance, and report preparation.
skill.summary: Plan, verify, and document authorized bug bounty testing with a structured security knowledge base.
skill.author: yangtech-gh

security_audit.summary: The skill is an explicitly dual-use offensive security guide with authorized-use and scope controls. Many alerts are Markdown false positives, but confirmed findings include privileged installs, persistent configuration changes, active scanners, cloud metadata targeting, system-file payloads, and executable exploitation guidance.

remediation.issue: The guide streams an unpinned release archive into tar without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a version and digest, download first, verify the checksum or signature, then extract only after explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: The skill can install scanners and packages with sudo.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for every privileged command and prefer isolated containers, virtual environments, or user-local packages.

remediation.issue: Third-party installers can modify agent and shell configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Show diffs before changing startup or MCP files, disable servers by default, and require confirmation before enabling commands.

remediation.issue: The knowledge base contains critical exploitation and credential-access payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Gate active payloads behind verified scope, redact destructive variants, rate-limit testing, and require human approval before each intrusive action.

remediation.issue: API keys are recommended in persistent shell and tool configuration files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a secret manager or per-command injection, enforce least privilege, and document restrictive file permissions and rotation.

content.value_statement: Bug bounty researchers need structured, scope-aware testing guidance. This skill provides methodologies, payload references, tool choices, and report templates for authorized engagements.
actual_capabilities: Maps web, API, authentication, business-logic, and MCP attack surfaces.
Selects vulnerability checks and payload patterns for common web security classes.
Compares proxies, scanners, AI hunters, and MCP security tools.
Provides installation and configuration guidance for referenced security tools.
Structures evidence, deduplication, severity reasoning, remediation, and final reports.
Defines scope manifests, rate limits, operating profiles, and authorized testing safeguards.
limitations: It does not verify legal authorization or program scope.
Payloads and commands may cause harm against production systems.
Third-party tools and latest-release downloads are not independently verified.
Results still require manual reproduction, impact validation, and false-positive review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Scoped Hunt
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized test plan from program scope, target surfaces, exclusions, and rate limits.

use_cases.title: Review Application Controls
use_cases.description: Build a focused checklist for authorization, authentication, APIs, workflows, and race conditions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Submission
use_cases.description: Turn verified evidence into a concise report with impact, reproduction steps, severity, and remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized testing checklist for [target type]. Include scope checks, safe starting steps, and evidence requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Testing Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare suitable tools for [surface]. Respect [constraints], minimize installation, and explain required permissions and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Vulnerability Candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this sanitized request and response for [vulnerability]. Propose minimal verification steps within [scope and rate limits].

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Engagement
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a deduplicated test workflow for [program]. Prioritize impact, enforce scope, define stop conditions, and specify human approval gates.

output_examples.input: Create a safe authorization testing plan for a multi-tenant API.
output: Define tenant roles, test accounts, permitted endpoints, exclusions, and rate limits.
Replay one verified request across accounts while changing only the object identifier.
Record response differences, affected data, and server-side authorization evidence.

output_examples.input: Outline a bug bounty report for a confirmed race condition.
output: State the violated single-use rule and affected endpoint.
Describe synchronized requests and the verified final server state.
Quantify impact and recommend atomic transactions with idempotency enforcement.

output_examples.input: Recommend a minimal reconnaissance setup without cloud keys.
output: Use local passive discovery, one scoped probing tool, and a shared deduplicated workspace.
Disable cloud integrations and unneeded MCP servers.
Confirm targets and rate limits before active requests.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization, encode scope once, and apply it to every tool.
Start passively, rate-limit active checks, and stop before destructive validation.
Reproduce findings manually, redact secrets, and report only verified impact.
anti_patterns: Do not scan assets that are absent from the approved scope.
Do not run privileged installers or third-party scripts without review and confirmation.
Do not submit scanner output without reproduction, deduplication, and impact validation.

faq.question: Does this skill authorize security testing?
faq.answer: No. You must obtain permission and follow the program rules before testing.

faq.question: Can it automatically exploit vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It provides actionable workflows and payload references, but intrusive actions require human approval and strict scope controls.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: No. Local and deterministic workflows are available, although some optional tools need provider keys.

faq.question: Which targets does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers web applications, APIs, authentication flows, business logic, race conditions, and scoped MCP or LLM features.

faq.question: Does it replace manual verification?
faq.answer: No. Every candidate finding requires reproducible evidence, impact analysis, and false-positive review.

faq.question: How should third-party tools be installed?
faq.answer: Review sources, pin versions, verify integrity, isolate execution, and confirm privileged or persistent changes.
